title: Police Broke In With a Warrant That Didn't Exist — Then What? #Shorts
description:
Police forced their way into a woman's home with a warrant that didn't exist — and searched everything she owned.

For most of American history, evidence taken in an illegal search could still be used to convict you. Then officers pushed into Dollree Mapp's home, waving a piece of paper they claimed was a warrant, and searched her entire house.

In 1961, the Supreme Court drew the line: evidence from an illegal search can't be used against you — in any state. This is general history, not legal advice.

Watch the full story on the channel.
